question: Why does a baseball umpire's strike zone shrink when the batter already has two strikes?
answer: Because a called third strike ends the at-bat, and umpires avoid being the one who decides it. Moskowitz and Wertheim, using pitch-tracking data, found the zone shrinks with two strikes and swells with three balls, when a called ball would hand the batter a walk. The umpire leans toward letting the players settle it.
move: When a call would be decisive, people quietly prefer to make no call.
ask: Which decision am I putting off only because making it would make me the one responsible?
reference: Tobias J. Moskowitz & L. Jon Wertheim, Scorecasting: The Hidden Influences Behind How Sports Are Played and Games Are Won, Crown Archetype, 2011
